title: Enterprise Control Plane Snapshot: Legal & Audit Brief
content:
Purpose:
This is a concise go-to-market briefing for sales & solutions on positioning Redwood's private control plane for regulated buyers (legal, audit, compliance leads). Focus: the language and artifacts that reduce stall risk during procurement and technical review.

Executive summary (one-paragraph):
Buyers in regulated industries care about three things: verifiable data flows, attestable controls, and predictable operational responsibility. For VPC/private deployments we must: (1) state exactly what Redwood runs (control plane components), what stays customer-managed (data plane, keys, network), and how we evidence that separation; (2) provide a compact, auditable evidence bundle tailored to common regulator asks; (3) give short remediation and incident scripts for legal/audit audiences. This brief gives scripts, evidence checklist, and objection rebuttals that sales/SEs can use in first two calls.

Key messages (speak plainly):
- Control plane is managed, telemetry is opt-in and can be routed only to customer-managed collectors.
- Customer data, model inputs/outputs, and KV caches do not persist in Redwood-managed storage unless explicitly enabled; default is ephemeral and in-customer VPC.
- Keys and secrets remain in customer KMS/HSM; Redwood never holds customer master keys.
- Audit trails: we provide signed, tamper-evident logs and can stream copies into customer SIEM or S3.
- Patch & change evidence: we provide release manifests, CVE mapping, and weekly cadence notes for private control plane components.

Evidence checklist (what to attach when a buyer asks):
- Architecture diagram (network flows, components labeled: control plane, data plane, admin consoles) — include egress/ingress arrows and telemetry toggles.
- Access control matrix & RBAC model for control plane admin roles.
- Sample audit logs: user-auth events, deploys, config changes (sanitized).
- KMS integration document and sample KMS policy.
- Pen test report summary + remediation timeline (redacted where needed).
- SOC2 type II statement and how it maps to control plane responsibilities.
- Upgrade/rollback runbook excerpt and SLOs for Private customers.

Buyer personas & suggested opening lines:
- Audit Chair / Head of Audit:
  - Opening: "We have an audit-oriented evidence bundle that maps every claim to a log or config — do you want the 1‑page mapping or the full pack?"
  - Concern: chain of custody, tamper-proof logs.
  - Quick rebuttal: we sign logs and provide push-to-customer-S3 plus an immutable index; we also support HSM-signed attestations on request.

- General Counsel / Legal:
  - Opening: "Here’s our standard data handling addendum and a short playbook for incident notice & litigation hold — can I highlight the parts legal teams typically want to change?"
  - Concern: liability for model outputs, e-discovery, data retention.
  - Quick rebuttal: contract side — we offer tailored DPA addenda, granular data retention controls, and e-discovery hooks (export APIs + canonical timestamps).

- CISO / Infosec:
  - Opening: "We configure the control plane to run behind your VPC and integrate with your SIEM and KMS — do you have a preferred logging stream?"
  - Concern: lateral movement, exfil risk, supply-chain.
  - Quick rebuttal: minimal network surface for control plane, zero-privilege operator model, signed manifests, reproducible builds for control plane components.

Common buyer objections + concise scripts:
- "If you manage the control plane, you can still access data."
  - Script: "We separate control and data plane. Control plane operates stateless orchestration and stores only operational metadata. Any customer payloads are routed through your VPC subnets and never persist on our managed instances unless you opt in. We can show you packet-level flow diagrams and a replay of a sanitized session.

- "We need absolute proof you didn’t touch keys."
  - Script: "We can integrate with your KMS/HSM so only you hold the customer master key; Redwood never has the capability to export it. We can provide a KMS integration checklist and a sample key policy used in production customers."

- "What happens in an incident?"
  - Script: "We notify per the contracted SLA, provide a forensics bundle (logs, config manifests, relevant snapshots), and, if requested, commit to an independent third-party forensic review. Our incident timeline templates show typical 48–72h triage and a 30‑day report cadence for enterprise pilots."

Incident scenarios and control-plane-specific guardrails (for legal/audit discussion):
- Scenario A — Operator mistake: wrong feature flag rolled into control plane.
  - Guardrails: canary-by-default, config signing, automated rollback, signed deploy manifests. Evidence: deploy manifest + rollforward timeline.

- Scenario B — Compromised operator credentials.
  - Guardrails: ephemeral operator sessions, MFA enforced via SSO, emergency certificate revocation path. Evidence: auth audit trail + revocation event.

- Scenario C — Data exfil via misrouted telemetry.
  - Guardrails: telemetry default-off, allowlist endpoints, VPC-only egress, encrypted streams to customer collectors. Evidence: network egress config + SIEM ingest proof.

Competitive notes (short):
- Large cloud providers (A/B clouds): claim "we already run it in your VPC" — gap: they often blur managed telemetry and may not provide signed attestations or a compact evidence binder for audits. Pitch against: packaged evidence and quick-run for auditors.
- Specialist on-prem inference vendors: claim total control but require heavy ops burden. Gap: longer time-to-pilot, fewer observability hooks. Pitch against: Redwood’s hybrid option gives faster pilot + developer ergonomics while meeting audit needs.
- LLM API providers (hosted): claim simplicity. Gap: cannot meet data residency and KMS control. Pitch against: emphasize separation and keys.

Pilot ask (what to request in the first technical pilot):
- 30–60 day technical pilot with defined success metrics: e2e latency target, token cost per thousand, audit evidence delivery within 7 days, integration into customer SIEM.
- Deliverables: private control plane instance in customer VPC (or in-customer private cloud), evidence bundle, runbook handover, and a 1‑page audit mapping doc.

Success metrics (audit/legal friendly):
- Evidence bundle completeness: all artifacts present and matched to claims (pass/fail check).
- Time to evidence: ability to produce requested logs/configs within contracted window (target: <72h).
- Integration sanity: SIEM ingestion validated and KMS integration tested (pass criteria).

Assets to attach to initial outreach:
- 1‑page control plane responsibilities map (single page).
- Sample audit mapping (control claim -> artifact).
- Mini runbook: incident notice & forensic timeline (2 pages).
- FAQ: 6‑8 legal/audit focused Qs and answers.

Sales play tips & red flags:
- Tip: always offer the 1‑page mapping first — audit chairs appreciate brevity.
- Tip: use signed artifacts as a differentiator in procurement conversations.
- Red flag: buyer repeatedly asks for unlimited access to Redwood consoles — escalate to solutions engineering; likely a trust boundary mismatch.

Open questions / follow-ups (TODOs):
- Add example HSM attestation template (Elena / infra).
- Confirm which release manifests we can share redacted (legal).
- Build a short video walkthrough of the evidence bundle for auditors (sales enablement).

Quick templates (copy-paste) — first outreach email (short):
Subject: Audit-ready control plane evidence — 1 page
Body: Hi [Name],
We have a 1‑page control plane responsibilities map and a short evidence bundle we share with auditors. Can I send the 1‑pager now and book 20 minutes to walk through the mapping?

If they reply yes — follow-up ask: Which SIEM/collector and KMS do you use? Any special compliance frameworks (HIPAA, FINRA, FedRAMP) we should map first?

Appendix — short glossary for legal/audit:
- Control plane: management/orchestration layer run by Redwood that never holds customer master keys and can be deployed in customer VPC.
- Data plane: where customer payloads are routed and optionally hosted entirely in the customer environment.
- Evidence binder: curated set of logs, manifests, policies and certs tied to specific trust claims.

Notes: this doc should be treated as a living sales artifact. Keep it short in client-facing form (1 pager + bundle). The longer pack is for auditor review only.

Document history: initial draft 2025-10-02 by Maya Park. Reviewed by Omar Singh and Elena Ruiz. Last edited 2026-02-25 (added incident scenarios and pilot ask).
